title: Patrol & Basic Motion
description: Move platforms, hazards, and AI enemies using Ping Pong Stepper, Enemy Chaser, Proximity Sensor, and transform tweens.

blocks.content: Not every moving entity is controlled by keyboard input. Lupis Engine provides [Ping Pong Stepper](node_library/helper_tool#node-pingPongStepper) for back-and-forth moving platforms, [Enemy Chaser](node_library/helper_tool#node-enemyChaser) for enemies that patrol and pursue the player, and tween nodes in [Animation](node_library/game_animation) for scripted motion.

items.title: Ping-Pong Platforms
items.desc: Oscillate an entity between **minPos** and **maxPos** on the X or Y axis and fire **onBounce**.

items.title: AI Patrol & Chase
items.desc: Patrol a set distance and automatically chase a tagged player within **detectRadius**.

items.title: Proximity Alerts
items.desc: Detect when a target enters or leaves a radius with [Proximity Sensor](node_library/helper_tool#node-proximitySensor).

items.title: Eased Tweens
items.desc: Animate position, rotation, and scale over time with **Move To**, **Rotate To**, and **Scale To**.

blocks.content: Choose the component setup that matches whether your [entity](components/entities_and_prefabs) is a scripted platform or a physics-driven enemy.

rows: Moving Platform / Hazard

[Transform & UI Transform](components/transform), a visual renderer, [Script Controller](components/script_controller), and a [Multi-Collider](components/multi_collider) (plus a **Kinematic (Scripted)** [Physics Body](components/physics_body) for solid platforms).
Patrolling / Chasing Enemy
**Physics Body** (**Dynamic**), **Multi-Collider** (**Solid**), **Script Controller**, and a player entity in the scene tagged **player**.

blocks.content: Build a back-and-forth moving platform using **Ping Pong Stepper** and a local direction variable.

items: Open your platform script in the [visual scripting](visual_scripting/graph_concepts) editor and create a **Local** **number** variable named **Dir** with a default value of **1** in [Variables & Collections](visual_scripting/variables_and_collections).
Add an [On Tick](node_library/game_lifecycle#node-eventTick) node and connect its **execOut** pin to a [Ping Pong Stepper](node_library/helper_tool#node-pingPongStepper) node.
On **Ping Pong Stepper**, set **targetEntity** to **self**, **axis** to **X Axis (Horizontal)**, **minPos** to **100**, **maxPos** to **400**, and **speed** to **2**.
In the [Property Inspector](interface/property_inspector), click **Switch to Variable** next to **direction** on **Ping Pong Stepper** and bind your **Dir (Local)** variable.
Hold **Alt** and drag **Dir** onto the canvas to create a **Set Dir** node, connect **onBounce** from **Ping Pong Stepper** to **execIn** on **Set Dir**, and wire **nextDirection** into **Value**.
Attach the script to your platform entity and click **Play** in the [Scene Viewport](interface/scene_viewport) to watch it patrol between X 100 and X 400.

blocks.content: To set up an AI enemy that patrols and chases the player, use **Enemy Chaser** instead:

items: Assign the **player** tag to your player entity in the **Object** section of the **Property Inspector**.
In your enemy script, connect **On Tick** to [Enemy Chaser](node_library/helper_tool#node-enemyChaser).
Set **playerTag** to **player**, **detectRadius** to **250**, **chaseSpeed** to **160**, and **patrolDistance** to **100**.

Optionally connect **movementState** and **facingDirection** from **Enemy Chaser** to [Platformer Animator](node_library/helper_tool#node-platformerAnimator) or [Top-Down Animator](node_library/helper_tool#node-topDownAnimator).

blocks.content: Tune these parameters on **Ping Pong Stepper** and **Enemy Chaser**.

rows: minPos / maxPos (Ping Pong Stepper)
Minimum and maximum world coordinate along the chosen **axis** (**x** or **y**).
speed (Ping Pong Stepper)
1 to 5
Position step added per frame along the chosen axis.
detectRadius / loseRadius (Enemy Chaser)
Distance in pixels at which the enemy starts chasing the player and gives up pursuit.
stopRadius (Enemy Chaser)
Distance from the player at which the enemy stops moving and fires **onInAttackRange**.
chaseSpeed / patrolSpeed (Enemy Chaser)
Movement speeds in pixels per second while chasing versus patrolling.
patrolDistance (Enemy Chaser)
Distance in pixels the enemy walks from its spawn point before turning around.

blocks.content: Combine motion nodes with tweens and sensors for richer level design.

rows: One-Shot Door or Elevator
Trigger [Move To](node_library/game_animation#node-tweenMoveTo) when a switch or [Trigger Zone](node_library/game_physics#node-triggerZone) fires, and choose **Smooth (Ease In-Out)** easing.
Enemy Attack on Range
Connect the **onInAttackRange** execution pin of **Enemy Chaser** to [Enemy Combat](node_library/helper_tool#node-enemyCombat) so the enemy attacks when it catches the player.
Turret or Trap Alert
Use [Proximity Sensor](node_library/helper_tool#node-proximitySensor) to fire **onDetected** when the player enters **radius** without moving the sensor entity itself.
**Ping Pong Stepper** stops at **maxPos** and does not reverse
Connect the **nextDirection** output to a local variable on **onBounce** and bind that variable to the **direction** input so the reversed direction persists across frames.
**Enemy Chaser** never detects the player
Check that your player entity has the exact tag matching **playerTag** (default **player**) in the **Object** section of the **Property Inspector**.
